name: security-pkcs11-object-policy-review
intent: PKCS#11 object attributes, sessions and permitted key operations
artifacts: Token/module version, session/login roles, key attributes/templates and wrapper operation policy.
trace: Trace lower-trust templates/handles into key creation, wrapping or use and determine whether operation attributes reflect the intended key purpose.
experiment: Use a local software token with synthetic keys and a reviewed operation sequence; compare allowed use and a policy-forbidden template/operation.
disproof: A key handle or token login is not export authority; do not extrapolate a software-token behavior to an untested HSM.
repair: Constrain object templates and role operations, testing legitimate key use, wrapping rules and lifecycle.
branch_decisions: Inspect session role, object class and CKA_SENSITIVE/EXTRACTABLE plus permitted usage/mechanisms; historical ALWAYS_SENSITIVE/NEVER_EXTRACTABLE attributes describe lifecycle constraints. Trusted wrapping and object templates can change effective policy. Software-token tests establish that implementation only, not physical HSM enforcement, and a permitted signature operation does not prove raw key extraction.
operational_method: Review C_CreateObject, C_CopyObject and C_SetAttributeValue separately. Retain CKA_COPYABLE/MODIFIABLE and the allowed transitions for sensitivity/extractability under the selected specification and module; making a key more restrictive differs from relaxing it, and historical attributes track lifecycle. Use disposable software-token keys only when that implementation is the test target. Compare allowed attribute changes with a denied relaxation; a signature operation is neither copying nor raw extraction.
